questions.modelAnswer: A fluid means a liquid or a gas — both flow and both exert pressure.

questions.stem: Explain why a submerged submarine's hull feels a squeeze from below as well as above.
questions.modelAnswer: A fluid at rest carries pressure to every point it touches, acting equally in all directions. The hull's underside faces fluid just as its top does, so the water pushes upward on the keel exactly as it pushes downward and sideways elsewhere — the squeeze has no favoured direction.

questions.stem: State the pressure-difference equation in symbols and name each quantity.
questions.modelAnswer: p = h × ρ × g, where p is the pressure difference in pascals, h the depth in metres, ρ the fluid's density in kilograms per metre cubed and g the gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram.

questions.stem: State how the pressure on an immersed object changes as it moves deeper.
questions.modelAnswer: The pressure rises as the object sits deeper, because the fluid column above it grows taller.

questions.stem: Explain why the pressure difference depends on the fluid's density.
questions.modelAnswer: The overlying column's weight creates the pressure at depth, and weight scales with mass per volume. A denser fluid packs more mass into the same column, so its weight — and the pressure it delivers — is larger for the same depth.

questions.stem: A diver measures a pressure difference of 20 kPa in fresh water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 N/kg). Calculate the depth, and state the rearrangement used.
questions.modelAnswer: Rearranged, h = p ÷ (ρ × g) = 20 000 ÷ (1000 × 9.8) ≈ 2.0 m, so the diver sits about two metres deep.
